MY LISTENING ADVENTURE

My Sound Patterns

Notice a repeating sound and describe its rhythm.

Look, then try.

Listen for a repeated call, tap or other comfortable sound. Draw marks or write words showing the repeats and pauses. If nothing repeats, make a gentle clap or tap pattern yourself and label it as your own. Keep imitation quiet and avoid disturbing wildlife.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

Stay with a grown-up away from roads, water edges and unfamiliar animals. Never follow a sound into an unsafe place. Listen indoors if needed. An adult helps cut cards. Keep claps and taps comfortable.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My repeating sound

Draw or write the sounds and pauses in order.

ACTIVITY 2

Copy it gently

Draw or describe a quiet clap or tap version.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

A sound pattern can repeat a group of sounds and pauses. Listening for repetition helps children notice rhythm and sequence.
